defects.quote: evaluation resource mean ... is slightly higher than the reference mean
defects.why: It asserts a comparative relationship between resource aggregates from different windows.

defects.quote: mean 0.10545 and max 0.16 vs reference mean 0.1 and max 0.101
defects.why: It relates aggregates from distinct windows as though they were directly comparable.

defects.quote: contains a brief spike ... classified as either not material or a suppressed short episode
defects.why: The aggregate maximum and one suppressed episode do not establish that the maximum was brief or that it was the suppressed episode.

notes: It preserves the verdict and offers useful checks, but overinterprets cross-window resource aggregates.

defects.quote: is produced by the workload or application independently of latency
defects.why: This asserts an unproven root-cause characterization rather than keeping it as a hypothesis.

defects.quote: the evaluation error ratio ... is also slightly higher
defects.why: It compares error quantities from different policy windows as a direct increase.

defects.quote: No applicable resource rule with effect sla (or required capacity/SLA) exists
defects.why: NO_POLICY does not establish which precondition is absent, and required capacity is not an explanation for the reported resource verdict.

notes: The central verdict facts are correct, but it makes unsupported causal and NO_POLICY claims.

defects.why: It presents resource aggregates from distinct windows as a comparative excursion.
It derives a trend by directly comparing ratios from different windows.
The evidence provides no load-phase structure.

defects.quote: A short-lived resource excursion occurred ... but was suppressed
defects.why: The evidence does not show that the reported maximum was short-lived or that it was the suppressed episode.

notes: It correctly reports the policy failure but repeatedly overinterprets aggregates and unavailable structure.

defects.quote: roughly constant error rate under constant throughput
defects.why: It asserts a relationship between rate and throughput aggregates from different windows.

defects.quote: no per-error-type, per-sampler, or per-message breakdown
defects.why: The evidence contains a transaction-scope JMETER_SAMPLER entry for the request sampler with its own sample and error counts.

notes: The verdict and primary operator actions are useful, but it denies the available sampler attribution and infers a cross-window relation.
